turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

"Hale. Meredith Kalinowski. I have until twenty to five, so let's use it."

She stays standing and sets her bag on the nearest desk.

"Owen found out about his zero from the gradebook, on his phone, in the middle of class. No one called me first. Who decided to post it before I was told?"
Be honest. On a scale of one to ten, how am I doing in this meeting?

"That's an odd question to put to a parent."

She glances at her watch, then back at you.

"But fine. A three. You asked me here, and I've asked you one thing: who decided to post that zero before anyone called me. You haven't answered it. Whatever you think of how this is going, I'd want your answer first.

Who decided, and when?"
And what's one thing I could do better?

"Answer the question I asked."

She doesn't sit.

"Who decided, when, and on what basis. Then put the paperwork in front of me: the checker's report with a date on it, the school's policy that lets you give a zero on a flag alone, and anything showing Owen was asked about it before the mark went up. I'll read every page.

Don't tell me what the checker said. Show me what it's based on.

I'll want all of it in an email afterward, too."
